topic.title: Preference Aggregation and Adaptive Information Elicitation
topic.overview: This topic combines uncertain judgments from people or models and decides which additional questions are worth asking. Workers may have partial knowledge, inconsistent reliability, or incentives that differ from the requester’s goals. Useful aggregation must therefore model more than a simple majority vote.
topic.whyItMatters: Expensive judgments should be allocated where they reduce uncertainty about the final decision. Interfaces that permit partial preferences and incentives that reward honest reporting can improve the information collected before any estimator is applied.
topic.evolution: Representatives include logarithmic opinion pooling in 1997 and later skill models, crowdsourcing quality control, and approval voting. Recent work studies selective aggregation, adaptive group queries, and information-driven Shapley estimation. These are distinct applications of learning from costly partial evidence, rather than one unified voting mechanism.
openQuestions: How can elicitation separate honest uncertainty from unreliable behavior?
Which adaptive queries improve decisions when judgments themselves change with context?
